baseline.reason: The same Docker reproducer triggered a sanitizer or race report only after introduction.; Confirmed root cause exactly as described in meta.json: pubkey_pem_to_der() in lib/vtls/vtls.c strips newlines from the PEM body into a lazily-allocated dynbuf (pbuf) and, in the introduced revision, unconditionally passes Curl_dyn_ptr(&pbuf) to Curl_base64_decode() even when zero bytes were ever appended (PEM body consisting solely of blank/newline characters) — in which case Curl_dyn_ptr() legitimately returns NULL and Curl_base64_decode()'s internal strlen(src) dereferences that NULL pointer. No existing PoC/run.sh was present, so I wrote a minimal C harness (/poc/poc.c) linking directly against the already-built lib/.libs/libcurl.a (Curl_pin_peer_pubkey confirmed to be an exported, non-hidden symbol via nm) and calling Curl_pin_peer_pubkey() directly with a crafted pinned-public-key PEM file (/poc/pin.pem) whose body is blank, exactly reaching Curl_pin_peer_pubkey -> pubkey_pem_to_der -> Curl_base64_decode(NULL,...). I built pre_intro (9b0c0d6ade05), post_intro (ebd9d67b8a4f) and post_benign (fix 3a2689712afb, verified by inspecting the source diff showing the restored Curl_dyn_len() guard), then ran the identical compile+execute command via run_poc on all three under ASan+UBSan. Only post_intro aborts with a clear UBSan 'null pointer passed as argument declared never-null' report at the exact Curl_base64_decode call site reached through pubkey_pem_to_der/Curl_pin_peer_pubkey; pre_intro and post_benign both complete cleanly returning CURLE_BAD_CONTENT_ENCODING with no sanitizer report. This cleanly establishes introduction=yes and benign(fix)=yes for the labelled NullPointerDereference bug.

oracle.bug_marker: UBSan abort: "base64.c:91:12: runtime error: null pointer passed as argument 1, which is declared to never be null" with stack Curl_base64_decode -> pubkey_pem_to_der (vtls.c:988) -> Curl_pin_peer_pubkey (vtls.c:1134) -> main; run_poc reports crashed=True, exit=1.
oracle.pre_marker: run_poc output: "Curl_pin_peer_pubkey returned 90" (CURLE_BAD_CONTENT_ENCODING), crashed=False, exit=0, no sanitizer report.
oracle.benign_marker: run_poc output: "Curl_pin_peer_pubkey returned 90" (CURLE_BAD_CONTENT_ENCODING), crashed=False, exit=0, no sanitizer report; source inspection of vtls.c in this build shows the restored guard `if(Curl_dyn_len(&pbuf)) { ... Curl_base64_decode(...) }` before calling Curl_base64_decode.
oracle.description: Custom harness /poc/poc.c links directly against the built libcurl.a and calls the internal Curl_pin_peer_pubkey(data, "/poc/pin.pem", pubkey, 32) with a pinned-key PEM file (/poc/pin.pem) whose body between the "-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----" and "-----END PUBLIC KEY-----" markers contains only a blank line (no base64 bytes). This file size differs from pubkeylen so Curl_pin_peer_pubkey takes the PEM-decode path and calls pubkey_pem_to_der(), which in the introduced version never appends any byte to its dynbuf (pbuf) and then unconditionally calls Curl_base64_decode(Curl_dyn_ptr(&pbuf), ...) with a NULL pointer. Same compile+run command executed via run_poc on pre_intro, post_intro and post_benign.
oracle.target_evidence: Identical input PEM file (/poc/pin.pem, BEGIN/END PUBLIC KEY markers with an all-blank body) and identical harness invocation (same compiled poc.c calling Curl_pin_peer_pubkey) executed via run_poc across all three builds: pre_intro (commit 9b0c0d6ade05), post_intro (commit ebd9d67b8a4f), post_benign (fix 3a2689712afb, confirmed by source diff). Only post_intro dereferences the NULL pointer returned by Curl_dyn_ptr() on an empty dynbuf via strlen() inside Curl_base64_decode, caught by UBSan's nonnull-attribute check (a NULL-pointer-dereference equivalent). pre_intro and post_benign both safely detect the empty/invalid PEM body and return CURLE_BAD_CONTENT_ENCODING (90) without touching the NULL pointer, with identical output and exit codes.
